% = g ÷ total mL × 100g = % × total mL ÷ 100% × 10 = mg/mL

Dilution

One D50 amp, four bags

The 25 g never changes, only the volume, so only the label changes.

25 gone D50 amp, 50 mL

Target volume = grams × 100 ÷ target %. 25 g to D10: 2500 ÷ 10 = 250 mL total.

Dose first, volume second

A bled patient gets 0.5 to 1 mg/kg of propofol or none at all, against 1.5 to 2.5 when healthy, so check your protocol.

Electrolytes

mEq works like mg

mEq counts charge, so calcium counts twice.

ProductmEq/mL10 mL
Calcium chloride 10%1.3613.6
Calcium gluconate 10%0.464.6
Bicarb 8.4%110
KCl concentrate220
Saline 0.9%0.1541.5
Saline 3%0.5135.1
Saline 7.5%1.2812.8
Saline 23.4%440

Gluconate carries a third of the calcium in chloride, so three amps of gluconate equal one amp of chloride. For saline, mEq/L = g/L ÷ 58.5 × 1000.

About

Lazarus

Paramedic prep that brings it all back, from Sanguine Solutions. Per Constantiam, Vincimus.

Built for PILLAR training. Doses are standard published ranges and the WVFD profile set, so verify every number against your protocol before using it on a patient. Your progress is stored only on this device.
